batch14: Batch fourteen of the barrier cream came back from stability and the pH had dropped 0.4 units over the test. The only thing we changed was the preservative supplier - same preservative, same percentage on paper. Turns out their grade has a different buffer in it. Nobody would ever see that on the label, the INCI list is identical. I need to write about this because customers think the ingredient list tells you what's in the jar and it doesn't tell you what grade, what supplier, what the raw material spec was.
cold_pressed: Had a call with a supplier who wanted us to put cold-pressed on the label for the rosehip oil. I asked for the process documentation and it turned out the oil was cold-pressed and then refined with heat, which kind of defeats the point for the fatty acids. It is technically true that it was cold-pressed. I think this is the thing people don't understand about label claims, a claim can be true and still not mean what you think it means.
layering: A customer wrote in saying our serum was pilling and making her skin feel tight. We went back and forth and it turned out she was putting the niacinamide serum on after an acid toner without waiting, so the pH on her skin was low when the serum went on. Once she waited ten minutes between them the problem went away. The order and the gap matter as much as the products and nobody tells people that.
barrier: The skin barrier is like a brick wall, the cells are the bricks and the lipids are the mortar. Everyone uses this metaphor. I think there is something more to say about it but I'm not sure what yet.
clean_beauty: Thinking about clean beauty again. It still annoys me that it means nothing. I've said this before though and I'm not sure what the new angle is. Maybe something about how people feel guilty using products that aren't clean. I want to write about this but I don't know.
